result:
32 of 33 pass; the one failure confirms a real bug in `Options`.

**Bug found:** `Options.hasShortOption(String)` (`Options.java:320`) is documented as testing whether the given **short** name belongs to an `Option` in this `Options`, but `addOption(Option)` (`Options.java:73-88`) always does `shortOpts.put(key, opt)` using `opt.getKey()`, which falls back to the long option name when there is no short name. So a long-only option (e.g. `new Option(null, "import", ...)`) ends up stored in the `shortOpts` map under `"import"`, and `hasShortOption("import")` incorrectly returns `true` even though `"import"` is not a short name. `testHasShortOptionFalseForLongOnlyOption` demonstrates this.

All other 32 tests pass, exercising `addOption` (all overloads, overwrite/chaining semantics), `addOptionGroup` (forcing group members optional, tracking the group as required), `addOptions` (merging, duplicate-key rejection, carrying option groups), `addRequiredOption`, `getMatchingOptions` (exact/partial/no match, hyphen stripping), `getOption`/`hasOption`/`hasLongOption` (hyphen stripping, null/empty/unknown handling), `getOptionGroup`, `getOptions`/`getRequiredOptions` (contents and unmodifiability), and `toString`.
